MATHEMATICS — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #7
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: MATHEMATICS
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which statement about 63 is correct? (1 mark)
   A. It is odd because it ends in 3
   B. It is even because it ends in 3
   C. It is neither even nor odd
   D. It is even because it has an odd number of digits

2. Which of these shows 604 in words? (1 mark)
   A. six hundred and four
   B. sixty-four
   C. seven hundred and four
   D. six hundred and forty

3. Which Roman numeral stands for 8? (1 mark)
   A. IIII
   B. VIII
   C. VIIII
   D. VX

4. Which statement about 1,357 is correct? (1 mark)
   A. It is even because it has an odd number of digits
   B. It is neither even nor odd
   C. It is odd because it ends in 7
   D. It is even because it ends in 7

5. In the number 4,835, the digit 3 is in which place? (1 mark)
   A. Thousands
   B. Ones
   C. Tens
   D. Hundreds

6. Work out 5,008 − 2,999. (1 mark)
   A. 3,991
   B. 2,019
   C. 1,909
   D. 2,009

7. Work out 6,120 − 3,845. (1 mark)
   A. 3,725
   B. 2,285
   C. 2,275
   D. 2,175

8. Work out 8,500 − 3,275. (1 mark)
   A. 5,375
   B. 5,235
   C. 5,125
   D. 5,225

9. A library had 4,250 books and 1,875 were borrowed. How many books remained? (1 mark)
   A. 2,375 books
   B. 2,365 books
   C. 3,625 books
   D. 2,475 books

10. A classroom has 13 rows of 12 desks. How many desks are there? (1 mark)
   A. 156 desks
   B. 146 desks
   C. 256 desks
   D. 136 desks

11. What is the next number in the pattern 2, 6, 18, ...? (1 mark)
   A. 36
   B. 20
   C. 24
   D. 54

12. Work out 48 × 21. (1 mark)
   A. 1,008
   B. 144
   C. 998
   D. 1,018

13. If ? × 9 = 63, then ? is found by (1 mark)
   A. 9 ÷ 63
   B. 63 × 9
   C. 63 ÷ 9
   D. 63 − 9

14. What is 84 ÷ 4? (1 mark)
   A. 31
   B. 20
   C. 21
   D. 22

15. What is 47 ÷ 5? (1 mark)
   A. 9 remainder 3
   B. 10 remainder 2
   C. 9 remainder 2
   D. 8 remainder 7

16. In the fraction 2/3, what does the numerator 2 tell us? (1 mark)
   A. How many of the equal parts are taken
   B. The number of wholes
   C. How many equal parts the whole has
   D. The size of each part in centimetres

17. Ali writes some more fractions. Which of these is an improper fraction? (1 mark)
   A. 1 3/4
   B. 5/12
   C. 3/8
   D. 7/4

18. Change 6 2/3 to an improper fraction. (1 mark)
   A. 18/3
   B. 20/3
   C. 21/3
   D. 8/3

19. Change 7/3 to a mixed fraction. (1 mark)
   A. 3 1/3
   B. 1 2/3
   C. 2 1/3
   D. 2 2/3

20. Beth writes some fractions. Which of these is a proper fraction? (1 mark)
   A. 2/9
   B. 11/5
   C. 9/9
   D. 3 1/2

21. In the number 0.74, the digit 4 is in which place? (1 mark)
   A. Tenths
   B. Tens
   C. Ones
   D. Hundredths

22. A hundred square has 82 of its small squares shaded. Which decimal shows the shaded part? (1 mark)
   A. 0.82
   B. 82
   C. 8.2
   D. 0.082

23. Which is the smallest number: 0.4, 0.44, 0.04, 0.404? (1 mark)
   A. 0.04
   B. 0.44
   C. 0.404
   D. 0.4

24. How many hundredths make one tenth? (1 mark)
   A. 1
   B. 5
   C. 10
   D. 100

25. Simplify 6p − p. (1 mark)
   A. 5p
   B. 7p
   C. 6p
   D. 6

26. What is 250 cm in metres? (1 mark)
   A. 25 m
   B. 0.25 m
   C. 2.5 m
   D. 2.05 m

27. What is 4 m 60 cm + 1 m 75 cm? (1 mark)
   A. 6 m 35 cm
   B. 6 m 25 cm
   C. 5 m 35 cm
   D. 7 m 35 cm

28. A box is 10 cm long, 10 cm wide and 10 cm high. What is its volume? (1 mark)
   A. 1,000 cubic centimetres
   B. 30 cubic centimetres
   C. 100 cubic centimetres
   D. 300 cubic centimetres

29. A learner says the volume of a cuboid 4 by 3 by 2 blocks is 9 because 4 + 3 + 2 = 9. What is her mistake? (1 mark)
   A. She forgot the corners
   B. She counted the faces
   C. She multiplied instead of adding
   D. She added the numbers instead of multiplying

30. A cuboid is 4 blocks long, 4 blocks wide and 4 blocks high. What is its volume? (1 mark)
   A. 68 blocks
   B. 64 blocks
   C. 16 blocks
   D. 12 blocks

31. How many 1/2 L bottles can be filled from 12 L of juice? (1 mark)
   A. 6
   B. 12
   C. 18
   D. 24

32. Which is the best instrument for comparing the mass of a mango with known masses? (1 mark)
   A. A beam balance
   B. A ruler
   C. A clock
   D. A measuring jug

33. On an analogue clock the short hour hand has reached or passed the number 7 but not yet reached the next number, and the long minute hand points to the number 9. What time is shown? (1 mark)
   A. 8:45
   B. 7:09
   C. 7:45
   D. 7:15

34. a.m. is used for times (1 mark)
   A. from midnight to noon
   B. from noon to midnight
   C. only at night
   D. only at midday

35. Lunch is at one o'clock in the afternoon. How do we write this time? (1 mark)
   A. 12:00 p.m. and 1:00 a.m.
   B. 1:00 p.m.
   C. 1:00 a.m.
   D. 1:00 noon

36. How many cents are in Ksh 5? (1 mark)
   A. 5,000 cents
   B. 105 cents
   C. 500 cents
   D. 50 cents

37. Kip faces North and makes a quarter turn anticlockwise. Which way does he face now? (1 mark)
   A. East
   B. West
   C. North
   D. South

38. Which everyday object has a face that is a circle? (1 mark)
   A. A brick
   B. A coin
   C. A door
   D. A roof end

39. A group of five tally marks is drawn by (1 mark)
   A. five separate circles
   B. two long lines
   C. four upright strokes crossed by a fifth stroke
   D. a square

40. Which is the safest way to count vehicles for a data project? (1 mark)
   A. Running alongside the vehicles
   B. Standing in the middle of the road
   C. From a safe place inside the school gate with a teacher
   D. Sitting on the road

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. A learner writes 5 in the mango row but the tally shows 4. Explain why this is a mistake and how to avoid it. (3 marks)

42. Name three objects in your classroom that have right angles. (3 marks)

43. A store stacks boxes 6 in a row, 3 rows deep and 2 layers high. How many boxes are in the stack? Give one safety rule for stacking. (4 marks)

44. Work out 6 1/4 L − 2 1/2 L. (3 marks)

45. Amina says the perimeter of a rectangle 8 cm by 5 cm is 13 cm. Explain her mistake and give the correct perimeter. (3 marks)

46. A vendor sells 2 bags of maize (m) and 3 bags of beans (b) on Monday, and 4 bags of maize and 1 bag of beans on Tuesday. (a) Write an expression for Monday. (b) Write an expression for Tuesday. (c) Simplify the expression for the two days together. (5 marks)

47. Explain why a table is better than raw data for answering questions. (3 marks)

48. Write the four facts that belong to an array of 3 rows with 8 dots in each row. (4 marks)

49. Draw a rectangle of 3 rows and 5 columns of squares. Write its area. (3 marks)

50. 38 mangoes are shared equally among 5 children. How many does each child get and how many are left over? (3 marks)

51. A school timetable shows assembly from 8:00 a.m. to 8:20 a.m. and mathematics from 8:20 a.m. to 9:10 a.m. Find how long each lasts and the total time. (4 marks)

52. Write the first five multiples of 9. (2 marks)

53. Find the volume of a cuboid that is 6 blocks long, 4 blocks wide and 3 blocks high. Show your working. (3 marks)

54. Njeri had Ksh 5,000. She bought a school bag for Ksh 1,850. How much change did she get? (2 marks)

55. A trip costs Ksh t for each pupil. Write an expression for the cost for 20 pupils and find the cost if t = 150. (3 marks)

56. A rectangle is cut into 12 equal parts and 5 parts are shaded. What fraction is shaded and what fraction is not shaded? (2 marks)

57. Bags of 5 kg are filled from a 50 kg sack of rice. Find the number of bags. (2 marks)

58. Njeri faces east. She makes two quarter turns clockwise, one after the other. Which way does she face? (3 marks)

59. A trader sold goods worth Ksh 3,568 on Monday and Ksh 2,276 on Tuesday. (a) Find the total. (b) Estimate the total by rounding each amount to the nearest ten. (c) How far is the estimate from the exact total? (5 marks)
pages.answers:
MATHEMATICS — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #7 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — It is odd because it ends in 3
   Look at the ones digit. 3 is odd, so 63 is odd.

2. A — six hundred and four
   604 = six hundred and four. Say the hundreds, then "and", then the tens and ones.

3. B — VIII
   8 is written VIII. Letters after a bigger letter are added.

4. C — It is odd because it ends in 7
   Look at the ones digit. 7 is odd, so 1,357 is odd.

5. C — Tens
   Counting from the right the places are ones, tens, hundreds, thousands and ten thousands. The digit 3 is in the tens place.

6. D — 2,009
   Subtract from the ones, regrouping when the top digit is smaller. 5,008 − 2,999 = 2,009. Check: 2,009 + 2,999 = 5,008.

7. C — 2,275
   Subtract from the ones, regrouping when the top digit is smaller. 6,120 − 3,845 = 2,275. Check: 2,275 + 3,845 = 6,120.

8. D — 5,225
   Subtract from the ones, regrouping when the top digit is smaller. 8,500 − 3,275 = 5,225. Check: 5,225 + 3,275 = 8,500.

9. A — 2,375 books
   Subtract 4,250 − 1,875 = 2,375. Check by adding: 2,375 + 1,875 = 4,250.

10. A — 156 desks
   Multiply to find the total. The answer is 156 desks.

11. D — 54
   The rule is multiply by 3. 18 × 3 = 54.

12. A — 1,008
   48 × 1 = 48 and 48 × 20 = 960. 48 + 960 = 1,008.

13. C — 63 ÷ 9
   To find the missing factor we divide the product by the known factor: 63 ÷ 9 = 7.

14. C — 21
   4 × 21 = 84, so 84 ÷ 4 = 21.

15. C — 9 remainder 2
   5 × 9 = 45 and 47 − 45 = 2. So 47 ÷ 5 = 9 remainder 2. Check: 9 × 5 + 2 = 47.

16. A — How many of the equal parts are taken
   The numerator is the top number. In 2/3 it says that 2 parts are taken.

17. D — 7/4
   In an improper fraction the numerator is equal to or bigger than the denominator. 7/4 is one whole or more.

18. B — 20/3
   6 × 3 = 18 and 18 + 2 = 20. The denominator stays 3, so the answer is 20/3.

19. C — 2 1/3
   7 ÷ 3 = 2 remainder 1. The whole number is 2 and the fraction is 1/3, so 7/3 = 2 1/3.

20. A — 2/9
   In a proper fraction the numerator is smaller than the denominator, so 2/9 is less than one whole.

21. D — Hundredths
   The first digit after the decimal point is tenths and the second is hundredths. In 0.74 the digit 4 is in the hundredths place.

22. A — 0.82
   82 out of 100 squares is 82/100 = 0.82.

23. A — 0.04
   Give every number the same number of decimal places and compare from the left. The smallest number is 0.04.

24. C — 10
   One tenth is 10/100, so 10 hundredths make 1 tenth.

25. A — 5p
   Only like terms can be joined. 6p − p = 5p.

26. C — 2.5 m
   1 m = 100 cm. Use this to change between the two units: 250 cm in metres is 2.5 m.

27. A — 6 m 35 cm
   Change to centimetres: 460 + 175 = 635 cm = 6 m 35 cm.

28. A — 1,000 cubic centimetres
   10 × 10 = 100 per layer and 100 × 10 = 1,000 cubic centimetres.

29. D — She added the numbers instead of multiplying
   Volume = 4 × 3 × 2 = 24 blocks.

30. B — 64 blocks
   One layer has 4 × 4 = 16 blocks. There are 4 layers, so the volume is 16 × 4 = 64 blocks.

31. D — 24
   Each litre fills 2 half-litre bottles, so 12 L fills 12 × 2 = 24 bottles.

32. A — A beam balance
   A beam balance compares an object with known masses.

33. C — 7:45
   Each number on the clock face is worth 5 minutes. The minute hand at 9 shows 9 × 5 = 45 minutes, so the time is 7:45.

34. A — from midnight to noon
   a.m. is used from midnight to noon and p.m. from noon to midnight.

35. B — 1:00 p.m.
   Times from midnight to noon use a.m. and times from noon to midnight use p.m. The correct answer is 1:00 p.m..

36. C — 500 cents
   Ksh 1 = 100 cents, so Ksh 5 = 5 × 100 = 500 cents.

37. B — West
   Going clockwise the order is North, East, South, West. Going anticlockwise it is North, West, South, East. North followed by a quarter turn anticlockwise gives West.

38. B — A coin
   A coin is round and flat, so its face is a circle.

39. C — four upright strokes crossed by a fifth stroke
   The fifth stroke crosses the first four to make a group of five.

40. C — From a safe place inside the school gate with a teacher
   Safety comes first. Count from a safe place and never stand in the road.

SECTION B
----
41. (3 marks)
   Answer: The number in the table must match the tally, otherwise the total will not add up correctly. Count the tallies carefully and check the total.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the mismatch, 1 mark for the effect on total, 1 mark for checking.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: Any three correct, for example a window, a door and a book.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct object.

43. (4 marks)
   Answer: 36 boxes. Put heavy boxes at the bottom (or do not stack too high).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 6 × 3 = 18, 1 mark for 18 × 2, 1 mark for 36, 1 mark for a sensible safety rule.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: 3 3/4 L
   Working / marking points: Change 6 1/4 to 5 5/4 (1 mark); wholes 5 − 2 = 3 and quarters 5/4 − 2/4 = 3/4 (1 mark); answer 3 3/4 L (1 mark).

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: She added only two sides. The perimeter is the distance all the way round, so we add all four sides: 8 + 5 + 8 + 5 = 26 cm.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the mistake, 1 mark for the reason, 1 mark for 26 cm.

46. (5 marks)
   Answer: (a) 2m + 3b (b) 4m + b (c) 2m + 3b + 4m + b = 6m + 4b
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for (a), 1 mark for (b), 3 marks for (c): 1 mark for adding the expressions, 1 mark for 6m, 1 mark for 4b.

47. (3 marks)
   Answer: A table puts the data in order under headings, is neat and easy to read, and shows totals. Raw data is untidy and easy to misread.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid point up to 3.

48. (4 marks)
   Answer: 3 × 8 = 24, 8 × 3 = 24, 24 ÷ 3 = 8, 24 ÷ 8 = 3
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct fact.

49. (3 marks)
   Answer: A drawing with 3 rows of 5 squares; area = 15 square units.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 3 rows, 1 mark for 5 columns, 1 mark for area 15.

50. (3 marks)
   Answer: Each child gets 7 mangoes and 3 mangoes are left over.
   Working / marking points: 38 ÷ 5 = 7 remainder 3. 1 mark for the division, 1 mark for 7, 1 mark for 3.

51. (4 marks)
   Answer: Assembly 20 minutes, mathematics 50 minutes, total 70 minutes (1 hour 10 minutes).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each duration, 1 mark for adding, 1 mark for 1 h 10 min.

52. (2 marks)
   Answer: 9, 18, 27, 36, 45
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the first three and 1 mark for the last two.

53. (3 marks)
   Answer: 72 blocks
   Working / marking points: 6 × 4 = 24 blocks in a layer (1 mark); 24 × 3 (1 mark); 72 blocks (1 mark).

54. (2 marks)
   Answer: Ksh 3,150
   Working / marking points: 5,000 − 1,850 = 3,150. 1 mark for the subtraction and 1 mark for the answer with Ksh.

55. (3 marks)
   Answer: 20t. When t = 150, cost = 20 × 150 = Ksh 3,000.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 20t, 1 mark for replacing t by 150, 1 mark for Ksh 3,000.

56. (2 marks)
   Answer: 5/12 is shaded and 7/12 is not shaded.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 5/12 and 1 mark for 12 − 5 = 7, so 7/12.

57. (2 marks)
   Answer: 10 bags
   Working / marking points: 50 ÷ 5 = 10. 1 mark for the division and 1 mark for the answer.

58. (3 marks)
   Answer: West
   Working / marking points: First turn east to south (1 mark); second turn south to west (1 mark); answer west (1 mark).

59. (5 marks)
   Answer: (a) Ksh 5,844 (b) 3,570 + 2,280 = Ksh 5,850 (c) 6 shillings more than the exact total
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for the exact total with regrouping, 1 mark for both rounded numbers, 1 mark for the estimate 5,850, 1 mark for the difference 5,850 − 5,844 = 6.
